<a id="a-chooser-reading-what-couples-in-its-rule-read-from-the-count-of-its-choices--读其所耦合者之择者其规则读自其所择之计数"></a>
# A chooser reading what couples in, its rule read from the count of its choices

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`capture-by-counted-choices` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](capture-by-counted-choices.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> A chooser choosing from a fold of what couples in selects through its couplings, and choosers sharing folds through pooled couplings; a rule read from the count of its choices, in sync under a standing score, never leaves the region its threshold sets and outlives an unread loss.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. The choice made from a fold of the prefix of what couples into a formation, whatever the fold and whatever the choice, is a selection through the formation's couplings up to each step; histories alike through the couplings are chosen alike, and with a part acting only beyond the coupling closure withheld, the rest of the exchange fixed and balance on what couples in, the choice is the same with and without the part. Near-definitional. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.foldAfter`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.selectsThrough`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.chosen_alike`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.unchosen_beyond_coupling`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* closure and balance; its declarations reach the grammar.
2. Choosers sharing their folds, each of a listed member's own course and the choice read off the list (a shared model built from all their prefixes among such choices), select through the group's pooled couplings; a part acting only beyond the pool's coupling closure does not change their choice. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.memberFolds`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.memberFolds_alike`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.pooled_selectsThrough`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.pooled_unchosen_beyond`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* closure and balance; its declarations reach the grammar.
3. A chooser over two policies takes the first where its rule weighs it at least as much as the second, and that policy's count rises by one; choosing by a favouring rule raises the share it reads, strictly, and choosing by a rule favouring the second strictly does not raise it; the rule read from the counts weighted by a standing score (κc, κo) is monotone in the share and favours the first policy exactly where κo · other ≤ κc · carrier. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.choose`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.choose_favoured`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.choose_unfavoured`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.choose_raises`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.choose_rises_strictly`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.choose_lowers`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.weighted`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.weighted_reads`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.weighted_favours_iff`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
4. Under a standing score, with the rule in force read from the counts at the start, along every schedule of reading the threshold κo · other ≤ κc · carrier divides the counts into two regions the course never leaves: at or above it the chooser takes the first policy at every step and neither the share nor the rule falls, also where the score favours the second policy (κc < κo); below it the rule favours the second policy strictly, the chooser takes the second policy at every step and neither the share nor the rule rises. Ties go to the first policy. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.start_locked`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.counted_locks`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.counted_chooses`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.lower_strict`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.counted_locks_down`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.counted_chooses_down`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* closure; its declarations reach the grammar.
5. Counted from the posterior at the time of choosing (selection by the fixed rule ⟨s + κc, s + κo⟩, the counts scaled with the posterior's weights added), a standing score favouring the second policy lowers the first policy's share strictly at that step, carriers present, and along a course at a positive fixed scale at every step; derived from RuleShaping. A falling share need not cross the threshold soon. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.byScore`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.posterior_count_falls`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.posterior_course_falls`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* no shared law's anchor among the constants its declarations use.
6. Joined to a coordinate that neither the counts nor the score reads, rising by at least one at every step, from counts at or above the threshold with the rule in force read from them the coordinate stands at least b + t at step t while the course stays locked and neither the share nor the rule is below its start. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.counted_outlives_loss`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* closure; its declarations reach the grammar.
7. Witnesses: three to one keeps the first policy against a score weighing the second twice as much; from one to one the score decides for good; one count moved, three to two, locks the other way; counted from the posterior at the time of choosing, three to one falls at the first step while the weighted rule still favours the first policy, by a tie, and favours the second from the second step. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.four_pos`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.counts`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.counted_beats_score`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.even`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.score_decides`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.moved`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.moved_locks_down`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.posterior_share_falls`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.after_one_still_first`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.after_two_turns`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* closure; its declarations reach the grammar.
8. Witnesses that the in-sync start is a hypothesis: counts three to one, above the threshold of the score one to two, under a rule an older score left in force (one to four), read at every step, lock the other way from step 5; a change of score to one to four read one step late, the old rule still in force, leaves the first policy locked from step 2, while read at once it locks the other way. (`Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.stale`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.above_but_stale_locks_down`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.above_but_stale_never_first`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.late`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.devalued_read_late_locks_up`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.devalued_read_late_keeps_first`, `Becoming.ChoiceCountCapture.Witness.Stale.devalued_read_at_once_locks_down`)
   - *Shared laws, by Lean dependency:* closure; its declarations reach the grammar.

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom and no premise beyond each law's own: for the selection laws, a reading of each step's values that reads exactly the formation's admission and the conditions coupled into it (ValuesThrough), and for the blindness laws the hypotheses of Flow.unselected_beyond_coupling and Flow.unselected_beyond_pool; for the count laws, discrete steps, natural counts with the second positive (RuleCapture's CarrierCounts), a choice taking the policy its rule weighs more with ties to the first, a standing score entering as two whole-number weights with the second positive, and the rule in force read from the counts at the start.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Any probability, surprisal, free energy or expected free energy: what is kept is any fold of what couples in, and the score two whole-number weights (board item UE2 carries conditioning and surprisal in counting form).
- Active inference's own scheme: it counts the end-of-trial posterior over policies, close to the executed policy where outcomes reveal it and split among policies that explain the trial equally; its prior is the counts' expected log, not the counts; it has a free-energy term, sampling and inferred precision. The threshold is the model's, not SPM's.
- That actual agents, brains or trained systems count their choices so or choose at the argmax; the overtraining effect the lock matches in rats has failed to replicate in humans (de Wit and others 2018).
- That the free-energy principle's partition into thing and world is a coupling structure of the World model: the selection laws read its sparse coupling, not its blanket condition, and no representation theorem joins a Langevin system with a Markov blanket to a web.
- More than two policies, intermediate precision, a score that changes with the outcomes, additive counting's timescale, and that a crossing under posterior counting comes within any horizon.
- That capture by counted choices is a loss or a gain: no evaluation enters, and ranking courses needs C or a premise in its place.
- **Counterexample:** A score is not enough to turn a count: three choices of the first policy to one keep it against a score weighing the second twice as much (Witness.counted_beats_score), while from one to one the score decides for good (Witness.score_decides). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ChoiceCountCapture.lean)
- **Counterexample:** The lock is not absolute: one count moved locks the course the other way (Witness.moved_locks_down), and a rule in force not read from the counts carries counts above the threshold the other way (Witness.Stale.above_but_stale_locks_down). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ChoiceCountCapture.lean)
- **Counterexample:** A falling share need not cross at once: counted from the posterior at the time of choosing, three to one falls at the first step while the weighted rule still favours the first policy, by a tie (Witness.after_one_still_first), and favours the second from the second step (Witness.after_two_turns). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/ChoiceCountCapture.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Active inference (Friston, FitzGerald, Rigoli, Schwartenbeck, O'Doherty and Pezzulo 2016, 'Active inference and learning', Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 68): the prior over policies counts beliefs about the selected policy at the end of each trial (§2.4; SPM12's spm_MDP_VB adds the end-of-trial posterior over policies); devalued after the habit has formed (trial 48) the habit persists and strengthens itself with repeated execution, devalued after 16 trials the agent switches at once (§5.2). The lock is the lock-in of increasing returns (Arthur 1989, The Economic Journal 99); counting the action taken is the value-free habit (Miller, Shenhav and Ludvig 2019, Psychological Review 126). Overtraining and insensitivity to devaluation in rats (Adams 1982; Dickinson 1985); five failures to induce it in humans (de Wit and others 2018, Journal of Experimental Psychology: General 147). The free-energy principle's sparse coupling read as the couplings; shared generative models (Friston and others 2024, 'Designing ecosystems of intelligence from first principles', Collective Intelligence 3) as pooled couplings at most. Its own laws restate; its third parts are related records: identical cells, risk minimization, what seeking cannot separate and a code held as counts. The readings are the AI's, in development/ue1-fep-bridge/NOTE.md, the review in REVIEW-UE1.md.
